title: Webhook delivery and duplicate events
body: A timeout does not prove that the receiver rejected an event. Read the delivery log and compare event IDs, attempt times, HTTP statuses and receiver acknowledgements. Retries may legitimately repeat an event ID; the receiver should use that stable ID for idempotency. Distinguish a delivery failure from duplicate business processing before proposing a change. Confirm that signature validation remains enabled; do not ask a customer to share signing secrets or disable verification. Escalate repeated 5xx responses with a redacted event timeline and request IDs. Do not replay, delete or modify events during initial investigation.

title: CSV imports and record totals
body: Keep the original sample unchanged. Check the expected header names, delimiter, encoding and required fields. Count valid, invalid and duplicate rows separately. A duplicate identifier must not silently increase the count of accepted records. Compare the import preview with source totals before assuming records are missing. Record a small redacted example and the validation message for escalation. Initial checks are read-only: do not overwrite the database, discard the source file or change existing stock or financial records.

title: Sign-in and access checks
body: Record the HTTP status and the affected operation. A 401 response indicates that valid authentication is missing; a 403 indicates that authenticated access may lack permission. Compare the sign-in time, expiry timestamp and requested scope without copying token or password values. Ask the user whether a fresh sign-in through the normal application page reproduces the issue. Establish whether one user or a wider group is affected. Escalate a reproducible permission mismatch with timestamps and redacted request IDs. Never request passwords, MFA codes, raw tokens or changes that weaken authentication.

title: Establish the scope of an incident
body: Separate reported facts from suspected causes. Capture the affected feature, first observed time and timezone, exact visible error and whether other users or features are affected. Check the published service status and recent release notes when those sources are available; their contents are not supplied automatically here. Record what has actually been checked and what is still unknown. A customer reply should acknowledge impact and ask focused questions without claiming that a fix or investigation has already happened. Escalate possible broad service impact for human review; a suggested priority is not an incident declaration.
